```{python}
#| label: fig-ic-tradeoff
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Transconductance efficiency $g_\\mathrm{m}/I_\\mathrm{D}$ (blue, left axis) and transit frequency $f_\\mathrm{T}$ (red, right axis) versus the inversion coefficient IC, calculated with the analytical model ($n = 1.3$, $L = 0.13\\,\\mathrm{\\mu m}$, $\\mu = 280\\,\\mathrm{cm^2/(V\\,s)}$). Weak inversion offers the best efficiency, strong inversion the highest speed."

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

n = 1.3
vt = 25.8e-3
mu = 280e-4      # m^2/(V s)
L = 0.13e-6

ic = np.logspace(-2, 2, 200)
gm_id = (1 / (n * vt)) * (1 - np.exp(-np.sqrt(ic))) / np.sqrt(ic)
ft = (1 / (2 * np.pi)) * 1.5 * mu / L**2 * vt * (np.sqrt(1 + 4 * ic) - 1)

fig, ax1 = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.5, 4))
ax1.loglog(ic, gm_id, 'b-', lw=2)
ax1.set_xlabel('IC')
ax1.set_ylabel('$g_\\mathrm{m} / I_\\mathrm{D}$ (V$^{-1}$)', color='b')
ax1.set_xlim(1e-2, 1e2)
ax1.set_ylim(1, 100)
ax1.tick_params(axis='y', labelcolor='b')
ax1.grid(True, which='both', alpha=0.3)

ax2 = ax1.twinx()
ax2.loglog(ic, ft / 1e9, 'r-', lw=2)
ax2.set_ylabel('$f_\\mathrm{T}$ (GHz)', color='r')
ax2.set_ylim(0.1, 1000)
ax2.tick_params(axis='y', labelcolor='r')

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```
